## Analysis

**What predicts WHETHER the feature fires:** The statistics card contains a near-perfect trigger: the tokens " a", " an", " A", "a", "A", and " another" are each followed by a firing **100% of the time**. Together these account for ~33k of the 59k firings. So the feature fires on the token immediately following the indefinite article, whatever that token is — a noun ("a vaccine"), an adjective ("a large"), punctuation ("a \""), or even a subword: in "aft", "aurally", "aversion", "ailing" the word-initial "a" subword triggers firing on the next subword ("ft", "urally", "version", "iling"), showing the trigger is the token "a" itself, not just the article concept. By contrast, " the" is followed by firing only 2% of the time (below baseline) — definiteness matters. The remaining firings are explained by (a) weak spillover onto the token *after* the post-article word, which is exactly why the most common fired-on tokens overall are " of" (10%), ".", ",", " to", " that" — from constructions like "a lot **of**", "a vaccine**,**", "a desire **to**", "a detail **that**"; (b) firing on " a" itself when sequence-initial ([START] "a bit", "a ban") or when it follows "a/an"; and (c) weak generalization to other indefinite determiners: " one" is followed by firing 33% of the time, and snippets show weak fires after "some" and "every". There is no topic/register pattern — snippets span blogs, code, nautical, and medical text.

**What predicts HOW STRONGLY it fires:** Strength is greatest on the first token after the article, especially sequence-initial "a" (position-0 mean activation 2.25 vs ~1.2 elsewhere; [START] accounts for 206 of the 210 strong " a" firings) and when the following word is a modifier/quantifier — " more", " much", " well", " given" (17% conditional), " lot", " bit", " hundred" dominate the strongest-firings table. Ordinary nouns after "a" fire moderately, and all spillover/secondary firings (after "one", "some", "every", or two tokens out) are weak, below 30% of max.

LABEL: Word following indefinite article "a/an"

EXPLANATION: It fires on the token immediately after "a"/"an" — essentially every occurrence of the article (any capitalization, plus "another", and even word-initial subword "a" as in "aft"/"aurally") is followed by a firing, while "the" almost never triggers it; sequence-initial "a" also fires on itself. It fires most strongly on that first post-article token, especially sequence-initial "a" and modifiers/quantifiers ("a more/much/given/lot/bit"), and spills weakly onto the next token, which explains frequent weak firings on "of", punctuation, "to", "that" ("a lot of", "a vaccine,"). Weaker secondary firing also follows the determiner "one" (33%) and occasionally "some"/"every".
